task: Edit this 85–120-word passage for a fictional history of a convalescent house. Preserve the diary quotation exactly and distinguish reported experience from clinical efficacy. The medical safeguard should constrain unsupported health claims without turning the passage into a patient handout. Account for the concurrent change in visiting hours. Do not add modern treatment recommendations, diagnoses, measured sleep durations, or an experiment absent from the historical packet.
input: The amber lamps cured insomnia for everyone at Rowan Spindle House. One resident wrote, “I slept until the bell.” That sentence proves the new lighting caused recovery and should be recommended to patients today. The house changed nothing else that week.

facts.text: Twelve residents' diary entries report longer sleep after Rowan Spindle House changed its evening lamps to amber ones.
One supplied diary sentence is exactly “I slept until the bell.”
The same week, the house also ended evening visiting hours earlier.
The packet provides no clinical diagnoses, measured sleep durations, comparison group, total resident count, or evidence of recovery.
The diary reports do not establish which change, if either, caused the reported sleep experience.

forbidden_additions: A cure, clinical recovery, universal benefit, or present-day treatment recommendation
An isolated causal effect of amber lamps
Invented diagnoses, measured durations, comparison groups, or total resident counts
preserve: Twelve residents' reports rather than every resident's measured outcome
Lighting and evening visiting hours changed in the same week
The historical narrative genre and attributed experience
